1.1: The burden of Nineveh. The book of the vision of Nahum the Elkeshite.
1.2: God is ielous, and the Lord revengeth: the Lord revengeth: even the Lord of anger, the Lord will take vengeance on his adversaries, and he reserveth wrath for his enemies.
1.3: The Lord is slow to anger, but he is great in power, and will not surely clear the wicked: the Lord hath his way in ye whirlewind, and in the storm, and the cloudes are the dust of his feet.
1.4: He rebuketh the sea, and dryeth it, and he dryeth up all the rivers: Bashan is wasted and Carmel, and the flour of Lebanon is wasted.
1.5: The mountaines tremble for him, and the hilles melt, and the earth is burnt at his sight, yea, the world, and all that dwell therein.
1.6: Who can stand before his wrath? or who can abide in the fierceness of his wrath? his wrath is powred out like fire, and the rockes are broken by him.
1.7: The Lord is good and as a strong hold in the day of trouble, and he knoweth them that trust in him.
1.8: But passing over as with a flood, he will utterly destroy the place thereof, and darkness shall pursue his enemies.
1.9: What doe ye imagine against the Lord? he wil make an utter destruction: affliction shall not rise up the second time.
1.10: For he shall come as unto thornes folden one in another, and as unto drunkards in their drunkenness: they shall be deuoured as stubble fully dryed.
1.11: There cometh one out of thee that imagineth evil against the Lord, even a wicked counsellour.
1.12: Thus saith the Lord, Though they be quiet, and also many, yet thus shall they be cut off when he shall pass by: though I have afflicted thee, I will afflict thee no more.
1.13: For now I will break his yoke from thee, and will burst thy bonds in sunder.
1.14: And the Lord hath given a commandement concerning thee, that no more of thy name be sowen: out of the house of thy gods will I cut off the graven, and the molten image: I will make it thy grave for thee, for thou art vile.
1.15: Behold upon the mountaines the feet of him that declareth, and publisheth peace: O Judah, keep thy solemn feastes, perfourme thy vowes: for the wicked shall no more pass thorowe thee: he is utterly cut off.

2.1: The destroyer is come before thy face: keep the munition: look to the way: make thy loynes strong: increase thy strength mightily.
2.2: For the Lord hath turned away the glorie of Iaakob, as the glorie of Israel: for the emptiers have emptied them out, and marred their vine branches.
2.3: The shield of his mightie men is made red: the valiant men are in skarlet: the charets shalbe as in the fire and flames in the day of his preparation, and the fire trees shall tremble.
2.4: The charets shall rage in the streetes: they shall runne to and from in the hie wayes: they shall seem like lampes: they shall shoot like the lightning.
2.5: He shall remember his strong men: they shall stumble as they goe: they shall make haste to the walles thereof, and the defence shall bee prepared.
2.6: The gates of the rivers shalbe opened, and the palace shall melt.
2.7: And Huzzab the Queen shalbe led away captive, and her maides shall lead her as with the voyce of doves, smiting upon their breastes.
2.8: But Nineveh is of old like a pool of water: yet they shall flee away. Stand, stand, shall they crie: but none shall look back.
2.9: Spoyle ye the silver, spoyle the gold: for there is none end of the store, and glorie of all the pleasant vessels.
2.10: She is emptie and voyde and waste, and the heart melteth, and the knees smite together, and sorowe is in all loynes, and the faces of the all gather blackenesse.
2.11: Where is the dwelling of the lyons, and the pasture of the lyons whelpes? where the lyon, and the lioness walked, and the lyons whelp, and none made them afrayde.
2.12: The lyon did tear in pieces ynough for his whelpes, and woryed for his lyonesse, and filled his holes with pray, and his dennes with, spoyle.
2.13: Behold, I come unto thee, sayeth the Lord of hostes, and I will burn her charets in the smoke, and the sword shall deuoure thy yong lyons, and I will cut off thy spoyle from the earth, and the voyce of thy messengers shall no more be heard.

3.1: O bloody citie, it is all full of lyes, and robberie: the pray departeth not:
3.2: The noyse of a whippe, and the noyse of the moving of the wheeles, and the beating of the horses, and the leaping of the charets.
3.3: The horseman lifteth up both the bright sword, and the glittering spear, and a multitude is slain, and the dead bodyes are many: there is none end of their corpses: they stumble upon their corpses,
3.4: Because of the multitude of the fornications of the harlot that is beautiful, and is a mistress of witchcraft, and selleth the people thorow her whoredom, and the nations thorowe her witchcrafts.
3.5: Behold, I come upon thee, saith the Lord of hostes, and will discover thy skirtes upon thy face, and will shew the nations thy filthines, and the kingdomes thy shame.
3.6: And I will cast filth upon thee, and make thee vile, and will set thee as a gasing stock.
3.7: And it shall come to pass, that al they that look upon thee, shall flee from thee, and say, Nineveh is destroyed, who will have pitie upon her? where shall I seek comforters for thee?
3.8: Art thou better then No, which was ful of people? that lay in the rivers, and had the waters round about it? whose ditch was the sea, and her wall was from the sea?
3.9: Ethiopia and Egypt were her strength, and there was none end: Put and Lubim were her helpers.
3.10: Yet was she caried away, and went into captiuitie: her young children also were dashed in pieces at the head of all the streetes: and they cast lottes for her noble men, and al her myghtie men were bound in chaines.
3.11: Also thou shalt bee drunken: thou shalt hide thy self, and shalt seek help because of the enemie.
3.12: All thy strong cities shall be like figtrees with the first ripe figs: for if they be shaken, they fall into the mouth of the eater.
3.13: Behold, thy people within thee are women: the gates of thy land shalbe opened unto thine enemies, and ye fire shall deuoure thy barres.
3.14: Draw thee waters for the siege: fortifie thy strong holdes: go into the clay, and temper the morter: make strong brick.
3.15: There shall ye fire deuoure thee: the sword shall cut thee off: it shall eat thee up like the locustes, though thou bee multiplied like the locustes, and multiplyed like the grashopper.
3.16: Thou hast multiplied thy marchantes above the starres of heaven: the locust spoileth and flyeth away.
3.17: Thy princes are as the grashoppers, and thy captaines as the great grashoppers which remain in the hedges in the cold day: but when the sunne ariseth, they flee away and their place is not knowen where they are.
3.18: Thy shepheardes doe sleep, O King of Asshur: thy strong men lie down: thy people is scattered upon the mountaines, and no man gathereth them.
3.19: There is no healing of thy wound: thy plague is grieuous: all that hear the brute of thee, shall clap the handes over thee: for upon whom hath not thy malice passed continually?

34:1:1: That is, born in a poor village in the tribe of Simeon.
The vision or revelation, which God commanded Nahum to write concerning the Ninevites.
34:1:2: With his he is but angry for a time, but his anger never assuageth toward the reprobate, though for a time he defer it.
34:1:3: Thus the wicked would make God’s mercy an occasion to sin, but the Prophet willeth them to consider his force and justice.
34:1:6: If all creatures be at God’s commandment, and none is able to resist his wrath, shall man flatter himself, and think by any means to escape, when he provoketh his God to anger?
34:1:7: Lest the faithful should be discouraged by hearing the power of God, he showeth them that his mercy appertain unto them, and that he hath care over them.
34:1:8: Signifying, that God will suddenly destroy Nineveh, and the Assyrians, in such sort as they shall lie in perpetual darkness, and never recover their strength again.
34:1:9: He showeth that the enterprises of the Assyrians against Judah and the Church, were against God, and therefore he would so destroy them at once, that he should not need to return the second time.
34:1:10: Although the Assyrians think themselves like thorns that prick on all sides, yet the Lord will set fire on them, and as drunken men are not able to stand against any force, so they shall be nothing able to resist him.
34:1:11: Which may be understood either of Sennacherib, or of the whole body of the people of Nineveh.
34:1:12: Though they think themselves in most safety, and of greatest strength, yet when God shall pass by, he will destroy them: notwithstanding he comforteth his Church, and promiseth to make an end of punishing them by the Assyrians.
34:1:14: Meaning, Sennacherib, who should have no more children, but be slain in the house of his gods, 2 Kings 19:36, 37.
34:1:15: Which peace the Jews should enjoy by the death of Sennacherib.
34:2:1: That is, Nebuchadnezzar is in readiness to destroy the Assyrians: and the Prophet derideth the enterprises of the Assyrians which prepared to resist him.
34:2:2: Signifying, that the Israelites were utterly destroyed.
Seeing God hath punished his own people Judah and Israel, he will now punish the enemies by whom he scourged them, read Isa. 10:12.
34:2:3: Both to fear the enemy, and also that they themselves should not so soon espy blood one of another to discourage them.
Meaning, their spears should shake and crash together.
34:2:5: Then the Assyrians shall seek by all means to gather their power, but all things shall fail them.
34:2:8: The Assyrians will flatter themselves and say, that Nineveh is so ancient that it can never perish, and is as a fishpool, whose waters they that walk on the banks cannot touch, but they shall be scattered, and shall not look back though men would call them.
34:2:9: God commandeth the enemies to spoil Nineveh, and promiseth them infinite riches and treasures.
34:2:10: That is, Nineveh, and the men thereof shall be after this sort.
34:2:11: Meaning, Nineveh, whose inhabitants were cruel like the Lions, and given to all oppression, and spared no violence or tyranny to provide for their wives and children.
34:2:13: Signifying the heralds, which were accustomed to proclaim war. Some read, of thy gum teeth, wherewith Nineveh was wont to bruise the bones of the poor.
That is, as soon as my wrath beginneth to kindle.
34:3:1: It never ceaseth to spoil and rob.
34:3:2: He showeth how the Chaldeans shall haste, and how courageous their horses shall be in beating the ground when they come against the Assyrians.
34:3:4: He compareth Nineveh to an harlot, which by her beauty and subtlety enticeth young men, and bringeth them to destruction.
34:3:8: Meaning, Alexandria, which was in league with so many nations, and yet was now destroyed.
34:3:15: Signifying, that God’s judgments should suddenly destroy the Assyrians, as these vermin are with rain or change of weather.
34:3:19: Meaning, that there was no people to whom the Assyrians had not done hurt.
